text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Parliament to begin full-time work in Berlin in 1999
- Tens of thousands demonstrate in Bonn against health reform
- Industrial production falls in October
- Shares and bonds surge
- White-collar union DAG wants pay rise in line with inflation
- Bankruptcies reach new record
HANDELSBLATT
- Substantial progress made on EMU stability pact
- One-third of all bankruptcies are in east Germany
- Firm dollar pushes Dax index over 2,900 points
- Federal states set to get compensation of eight billion marks for loss of wealth tax
- Audi boss Demel goes to Brazil for VW
- Thyssen streamlines its telecoms business
- U.S. court allows further case against VW
- Bankruptcies set to continue at record levels until 2000
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Broad resistance against health reform
- Health minister ignored demands for tighter checks on veterinary drug approval
- Tax authorities to scrutinise top earners more carefully
- Programme to encourage RAF left-wing guerrillas to give up will be continued
- Scepticism about EMU pushes dollar over 1.57 marks
- Analysts doubt Bonn's projection of two percent growth in 1997
- Deutsche Bahn AG to invest 81 billion marks over five years
- Tietmeyer would like to retire in 1999
- VW suffers another blow in court battle against GM
- Bundesbank dampens speculation of another rate cut
- Bankruptcies to continue at record level into year 2000
DIE WELT
- Protesters march against health reforms
- Kohl and Czech premier Klaus largely in agreement over joint declaration
- More confusion over parliament's move to Berlin
- First signs of compromise between VW and Opel
- Court outlaws confectionery industry strike
- 1997 to bring no relief to jobs market
- SPD takes hard line in row over wealth tax
- No agreement yet on EMU stability pact
- German shares continue to set new records
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
